A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: Section 5, Tables 1–3, and Figure 1 report original sampler experiments on Bayesian and synthetic targets, including diffusion-coefficient ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original results on 100-dimensional GMM-40 and MoS-10 targets in Appendix B, Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The rKL-LD gradient estimator, control variate, DBS/CMCD parameterizations, and learnable diffusion coefficients are retained. The added pseudocode documents existing loss computations without establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds GMM-40 and MoS-10 evaluations at 100 dimensions, extending the existing 50-dimensional mixture scenarios. The Bayesian targets, Funnel, Many Well, and original mixture evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership. The added higher-dimensional experiments reuse the existing DBS/CMCD and rKL-R/LV comparison families without introducing a new baseline.

E3.justification: Tables 4–5 introduce log Z as an additional reported evaluation quantity. The original experiments retain their stated training budgets, diffusion steps, sample sizes, and checkpoint-selection procedures.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the learned-versus-fixed diffusion-coefficient ablation to GMM-40 at 100 dimensions, adding evidence about whether its benefits persist in this harder setting. The original Brownian/Seeds sensitivity analyses and Figure 1 are unchanged.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix C.1 and v2 Appendix D.1 retain the same seed counts, standard-error reporting, and repeated metric evaluations. The new tables continue reporting values with uncertainty without documenting a new statistical procedure or increased run counts.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically unchanged, but Tables 4–5 add substantial 100-dimensional comparisons across five metrics, including log Z and severe LV instability. For example, GMM-40 (100d) CMCD-LV with fixed coefficients reports ELBO approximately -1.96 × 10^9. These are additional-setting results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds a continuous-domain counterexample to the LV data processing inequality, with mutually absolutely continuous distributions and an analytic derivation in Appendix A.6.1. The original discrete counterexample survives as A.6.2. Section 2.3.1 also adds a support condition to the statement that zero LV implies equal distributions.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient nonequivalence, LV's failure of the data processing inequality, rKL-LD performance, and learnable diffusion coefficients. The additions supply evidence for existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds discussion of the stability-versus-gradient-bias tradeoff for Langevin stop-gradients in A.1 and interprets the higher-dimensional results in Appendix B. Its new statement that learned coefficients consistently help is too broad: Table 4 reports CMCD ELBO -45.10 with fixed coefficients versus -45.84 with learned coefficients.

D1.justification: V2 adds a direct code-repository link and three pseudocode algorithms specifying path detachment, batch control variates, and backpropagation. Existing architecture and hyperparameter documentation largely survives. The new algorithms specify Adam, conflicting with the retained RAdam specification in D.3; this does not establish an actual optimizer change.

R1.justification: The bibliography and main related-work section retain the same works. Appendix A.1 adds a limited discussion attributing a Langevin stop-gradient stabilization approach to the already-cited Vargas et al. (2023) and identifying its gradient-bias tradeoff.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. V2 makes localized terminology and explanation edits, updates affiliations/contact information, subdivides the counterexample appendix, and adds experimental, pseudocode, and checklist sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the NeurIPS template with redesigned front matter, headings, and reflowed displays. It adds a prominent boxed continuous counterexample with a variance plot, two result tables, and three algorithm blocks. The original Figure 1 and Tables 1–3 remain.

improvement.justification: The continuous-domain proof strengthens the central theoretical argument, while the higher-dimensional evaluations, pseudocode, and code link improve assessment and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by Appendix B's overstatement of learned-coefficient benefits relative to Table 4 and the new Adam/RAdam documentation inconsistency.
